roadmap.goal: A Process Behaviour Chart must never call a baseline 'in the future' just because the viewer's calendar day is ahead of the instance's. Today, a Team or Portfolio with no configured baseline uses the display window (ending on the viewer's local today) as its baseline and runs it through BaselineValidationService.Validate, whose 'end must not be in the future' rule is anchored on the instance day (Clock.Today). Between local midnight and instance midnight every PBC of a viewer ahead of the instance zone renders BaselineInvalid (CI: Europe/Zurich browser vs UTC backend, 22:00-24:00 UTC; the Throughput PBC also loses its forecast-filter toggle). The baseline picker in settings has the mirror defect: its max is the UTC day, while the server judges the end against the instance day, which the browser cannot know. Fix: (1) the implicit baseline (display window) skips the future-end rule and keeps every other rule; (2) a configured baseline may end at most one day after the instance day, on save and at render, so any viewer may pick their own today; anything two or more days ahead stays refused; (3) the picker's max is the viewer's local today; (4) the four duplicated resolve-and-validate blocks become one helper. Acceptance: new regression tests RED before and GREEN after; full backend suite (minus live-connector categories) and frontend suite + build stay GREEN; Stryker per-feature kill rate >= 80% on the touched methods.

criteria: Public Validate(start, end, doneItemsCutoffDays, today) keeps its signature (four controllers and the services call it). Its future rule refuses only an end more than one day after `today`; an end of today+1 is valid, today+2 is invalid with a message containing 'future'. The existing Validate_EndDateInFuture_ReturnsInvalid (+5 days) stays green unchanged.
New public ValidateDisplayWindowAsBaseline(DateTime start, DateTime end, int doneItemsCutoffDays, DateOnly today) runs every rule except the future-end rule.
No public method takes a bool flag (Sonar S2360/S3242 family): the two public entry points share a private core.
RED tests fail against the current code for the stated reason (valid expected, invalid 'future' returned) and the RED output is recorded before GREEN.

Any comment states the why in plain words, e.g. that the browser cannot know the instance's day and a viewer's today is at most one day ahead of it; no internal references (no RC-A, no bug numbers outside a pragma).
